Uncertainty in human life gives rise to the need for legal and economic protection instruments, one of which is through the insurance mechanism. As a form of risk transfer, insurance provides compensation guarantees for losses due to uncertain events, such as accidents, fires, or death. In the legal framework in Indonesia, the relationship between the insurer and the insured is formed through an agreement (policy) or normative provisions in laws and regulations. However, in practice, this relationship is inseparable from the problem of moral hazard, especially the misuse of claims by the insured who act dishonestly. This phenomenon not only causes economic losses for insurance companies, but also threatens the integrity of the insurance system itself. Therefore, an effective legal protection mechanism is needed for insurance companies to deal with these manipulative practices. This paper examines the forms of legal protection available, both through contractual instruments (internal) and external regulations such as Law Number 40 of 2014 concerning Insurance. With a normative legal approach, this paper aims to provide a deeper understanding of the importance of maintaining a balance of rights and obligations in insurance contracts and the need to strengthen legal aspects in anticipating misuse of claims.

Insurance has been an important part of the Indian financial system. Life insurance in India is a growth oriented industry. In the year 2000, life insurance industry has been liberalized after more than 50 years of monopoly with LIC. During the period of 13 years after liberalization, private life insurances have launched many innovations in the industry and it is at this juncture it has become imperative to study the profitability performance of these companies. Five life insurance companies have been selected for the study.

data.Documented value: Cyber operational risk scenarios for insurance companies

Abstract Cyber Operational Risk: Cyber risk is routinely cited as one of the most important sources of operational risks facing organisations today, in various publications and surveys. Further, in recent years, cyber risk has entered the public conscience through highly publicised events involving affected UK organisations such as TalkTalk, Morrisons and the NHS. Regulators and legislators are increasing their focus on this topic, with General Data Protection Regulation (“GDPR”) a notable example of this. Risk actuaries and other risk management professionals at insurance companies therefore need to have a robust assessment of the potential losses stemming from cyber risk that their organisations may face. They should be able to do this as part of an overall risk management framework and be able to demonstrate this to stakeholders such as regulators and shareholders. Given that cyber risks are still very much new territory for insurers and there is no commonly accepted practice, this paper describes a proposed framework in which to perform such an assessment. As part of this, we leverage two existing frameworks – the Chief Risk Officer (“CRO”) Forum cyber incident taxonomy, and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (“NIST”) framework – to describe the taxonomy of a cyber incident, and the relevant cyber security and risk mitigation items for the incident in question, respectively.Summary of Results: Three detailed scenarios have been investigated by the working party: ∙ Employee leaks data at a general (non-life) insurer: Internal attack through social engineering, causing large compensation costs and regulatory fines, driving a 1 in 200 loss of £210.5m (c. 2% of annual revenue). ∙ Cyber extortion at a life insurer: External attack through social engineering, causing large business interruption and reputational damage, driving a 1 in 200 loss of £179.5m (c. 6% of annual revenue). ∙ Motor insurer telematics device hack: External attack through software vulnerabilities, causing large remediation / device replacement costs, driving a 1 in 200 loss of £70.0m (c. 18% of annual revenue). Limitations: The following sets out key limitations of the work set out in this paper: ∙ While the presented scenarios are deemed material at this point in time, the threat landscape moves fast and could render specific narratives and calibrations obsolete within a short-time frame. ∙ There is a lack of historical data to base certain scenarios on and therefore a high level of subjectivity is used to calibrate them.

sections.heading: LEGAL PROTECTION FOR INSURANCE COMPANIES AGAINST ABUSE OF INSURANCE CLAIMS
paragraphs: ### Legal Protection for Insurance Companies Against Abuse of Insurance Claims [[S1|documented source evidence]] In the realm of insurance, the relationship between insurers and insureds is often fraught with potential for abuse. This phenomenon, known as moral hazard, can lead to significant economic losses for insurance companies and undermine the integrity of the insurance system. As a form of risk transfer, insurance compensates for losses due to uncertain events such as accidents, fires, or death. However, in practice, this relationship is often intertwined with the issue of moral hazard, particularly the misuse of claims by insured individuals who act dishonestly.

This paper examines the forms of legal protection available to insurance companies to address these manipulative practices. [[S1|documented source evidence]] The legal framework in Indonesia provides a balance of rights and obligations in insurance contracts, but it is not always sufficient to prevent misuse of claims. This paper aims to provide a deeper understanding of the importance of maintaining a balance of rights and obligations in insurance contracts and the need to strengthen legal aspects in anticipation of such misuse. Through a normative legal approach, this paper explores the forms of legal protection available, both through contractual instruments (internal) and external regulations such as Law Number 40 of 2014 concerning Insurance.

[[S1|documented source evidence]] ### Factors Affecting the Financial Health of General Insurance Companies and Life Insurance Companies in Indonesia [[S1|documented source evidence]] This study analyzes the factors that affect the level of financial health of general insurance companies and life insurance companies in Indonesia. The research employs logistic regression analysis and survival analysis to determine the impact of various factors on the financial health of these companies. The results of the analysis reveal that the return on assets has a negative influence on the non-fulfillment of financial health for life insurance companies or the general public. Conversely, the claim ratio has a positive influence on the financial health of the insurance company.

In life insurance companies, the placement of insurance in bond instruments or debt securities has a negative effect on the non-fulfillment of the financial health condition of the insurance company. The findings from the logistic regression and survival analysis for life insurance companies are consistent, but the results from the survival analysis for general insurance companies are biased. This study contributes to understanding insolvency risks in emerging-market insurance systems using dual-model analysis, offering practical implications for regulators and practitioners in developing economies with limited policyholder protection mechanisms. [[S1|documented source evidence]] ### Conclusion [[S1|documented source evidence]] The legal protection of insurance companies against abuse of insurance claims is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the insurance system.
By understanding the mechanisms and limitations of legal protection, insurers can better manage risks and ensure that their financial health is protected. [[S1|documented source evidence]]

paragraphs: ### Best Life Insurance Companies for Seniors in India [[S2|documented source evidence]]

Life insurance is a crucial tool for protecting against financial loss, offering a means to manage risk. In India, the life insurance industry has been growing rapidly, driven by the liberalization of the sector in 2000. This period saw the launch of numerous innovations, making it imperative to analyze the profitability of these companies. [[S2|documented source evidence]]

Five life insurance companies have been selected for this study: ICICI Prudential, HDFC Life, Reliance Life, Axis Life, and LIC. These companies have been chosen for their significant market share and reputation in the Indian life insurance industry. The study aims to assess their profitability performance, which is crucial for understanding their financial health and future prospects. [[S2|documented source evidence]]

The profitability of these companies is influenced by various factors, including their ability to manage risk, capital adequacy, and reinsurance support. The study will delve into these aspects to provide a comprehensive understanding of their financial performance. [[S2|documented source evidence]]
### Supply and Demand Imbalances in the Indonesian Life Insurance Industry [[S2|documented source evidence]]

In Indonesia, the life insurance industry has faced significant challenges in providing adequate life insurance protection for retirees. The retired group is considered high risk due to age and health factors, making it difficult for them to obtain life insurance protection from insurance companies. This scarcity of life insurance protection is a major concern, as it affects the retirement savings of many individuals. [[S2|documented source evidence]]

The research method used in this study is an explanatory quantitative approach, combining surveys of insurance companies and financial institutions with mediation analysis (moral hazard) and moderation (fraud and risk management capacity). The results of the study highlight that supply-demand imbalances, high claims ratios, limited capital, and weak reinsurance support are the main factors causing the scarcity of life insurance protection for retirees' credit. [[S2|documented source evidence]]

The role of moral hazard and fraud also increases the risk of a scarcity of protection. This study concludes that collaboration between insurance companies, banks, and regulators is essential to create an inclusive and sustainable life insurance protection model for the retiree segment. [[S2|documented source evidence]]
### Conclusion [[S2|documented source evidence]]

The profitability of life insurance companies in India is influenced by various factors, including their ability to manage risk, capital adequacy, and reinsurance support. The study of these companies' financial performance is crucial for understanding their financial health and future prospects. The scarcity of life insurance protection for retirees in Indonesia highlights the importance of collaboration between insurance companies, banks, and regulators to create an inclusive and sustainable life insurance protection model for the retiree segment. [[S2|documented source evidence]]

sections.heading: Analysis of Factors Affecting the Financial Health of General Insurance
paragraphs: ### Analysis of Factors Affecting the Financial Health of General Insurance and Life Insurance Companies in Indonesia [[S4|documented source evidence]] The financial health of insurance companies is a crucial factor for their stability and profitability. This study aims to analyze the factors that influence the financial health of general insurance companies and life insurance companies in Indonesia. The research employs logistic regression analysis and survival analysis to provide a comprehensive understanding of these factors. [[S4|documented source evidence]] ### Logistic Regression Analysis [[S4|documented source evidence]] Logistic regression analysis reveals that the return on assets has a significant negative influence on the non-fulfillment of the financial health of life insurance companies or the general public.

This suggests that companies with higher asset returns are less likely to meet financial health standards. Conversely, a positive claim ratio is associated with better financial health, indicating that companies with lower claim ratios are more likely to maintain their financial stability. [[S4|documented source evidence]] ### Survival Analysis [[S4|documented source evidence]] Survival analysis, on the other hand, provides insights into the financial health of general insurance companies. The results indicate that the placement of insurance in bond instruments or debt securities has a negative effect on the non-fulfillment of the financial health condition of the insurance company.

This suggests that companies that invest heavily in these instruments are more likely to face financial difficulties. [[S4|documented source evidence]] ### Life Insurance Companies [[S4|documented source evidence]] In life insurance companies, the results of the survival analysis produced for life insurance companies are biased. This suggests that the survival analysis may not be the most reliable method for assessing the financial health of life insurance companies. However, the results obtained from logistic regression analysis for life insurance companies are not much different, indicating that the method used is consistent across different sectors.

[[S4|documented source evidence]] ### Implications and Limitations [[S4|documented source evidence]] For the fourth evidence section on Analysis of Factors Affecting the Financial Health of General Insurance, this boundary is especially relevant: this study contributes to understanding insolvency risks in emerging-market insurance systems using dual-model analysis, offering practical implications for regulators and practitioners in developing economies with limited policyholder protection mechanisms. The results highlight the need for different approaches to portfolio regulations for life insurance and pension funds, emphasizing the importance of prudent person rules in certain circumstances.
